name: LinkedIn Profile Analysis - UX Designer
description: Signals extracted from LinkedIn profiles to evidence UX Designer skills. LinkedIn provides professional context, endorsements, recommendations, published case studies, and career progression data. NOTE: Specific evidence mappings (maps_to composite keys) are stored within individual skill files under evidence.linkedin, NOT here.

headline_summary.notes: Look for behavioral design specialization in headline (e.g., 'Behavioral UX Designer', 'Product Designer | Persuasive Tech', 'UX Lead | Behavioral Economics'). Generic 'UX Designer' provides minimal signal.
quality_indicators: Explicit behavioral design specialization in headline
Framework references in summary (Fogg, Hook Model, JTBD)
Portfolio link in featured or contact section

experience.notes: Similar to CV work experience. Prioritize descriptions of behavioral impact and framework application over tool listings.
quality_indicators: UX-specific job titles (UX Designer, Product Designer, Interaction Designer, Behavioral Designer, UX Researcher)
Duration and continuity in UX/behavioral design roles
Company context (fintech, healthtech, edtech, B2C apps — domains where behavioral design has highest impact)
Quantified behavioral outcomes (retention lift, conversion increase, activation improvement)

skills_endorsements.notes: UX skill endorsements have low evidential value. Figma endorsements are near-universal and carry minimal signal. Behavioral Economics or Persuasive Design endorsements are rarer and more meaningful.

projects.notes: Projects section with portfolio links or Figma embeds provide strong supporting evidence. Look for case study depth.
quality_indicators: Links to Figma case studies or Behance/Dribbble portfolios
Described behavioral design rationale in project descriptions
Cross-functional project context (worked with engineers, PMs, behavioral scientists)

recommendations.notes: Recommendations from product managers, engineers, or behavioral scientists that specifically cite the designer's behavioral design impact or framework expertise are strong third-party validation.
quality_indicators: Recommendation from PM or engineer citing specific behavioral design contribution
Mention of measurable impact (retention, conversion, engagement)
Reference to expertise in behavioral frameworks or persuasive design

posts_articles.notes: LinkedIn articles on behavioral design, persuasive UX, gamification, or behavioral economics indicate deep subject matter expertise. Posts sharing design case studies with behavioral rationale are high-signal.
quality_indicators: Articles or posts specifically about behavioral design, Fogg, Hook Model, or nudge theory
Case study posts with behavioral design rationale and outcomes
Engagement (comments, reactions) indicating community recognition of expertise

patterns.pattern: UX Design, User Experience Design, or Interaction Design endorsed
Behavioral Design, Persuasive Technology, or Behavior Change Design endorsed
A/B Testing, Conversion Optimization, or Experimentation endorsed
Figma, Adobe XD, Sketch, or Balsamiq endorsed
Gamification, Engagement Design, or Retention Design endorsed or mentioned
Journey Mapping, Service Design, or Customer Experience endorsed
Business analysis, BPMN, or process modeling mentioned

important_notes: A portfolio link in the LinkedIn profile is equivalent to a strong project reference — always evaluate linked portfolio case studies
LinkedIn is weaker evidence for UX than GitHub/portfolio for engineering roles — the behavioral UX skills that matter most (framework application, A/B testing) rarely leave code artifacts
High endorsement counts for generic skills (Figma, UX Design) add minimal signal — look for specificity of behavioral design skills endorsed
Recommendations that quantify behavioral design impact (retention %, conversion lift) are the strongest LinkedIn evidence category for UX
